newsitem.title: USA: Top FCC officials move to block liquor-ad probe.
newsitem.headline: Top FCC officials move to block liquor-ad probe.

text.p: A bid by the nation's top communications regulator to open a probe into liquor advertising on television hit a setback Thursday after two fellow regulators sought to block the move.

Commissioners Rachelle Chong and James Quello of the Federal Communications Commission said an investigation was outside the agency's jurisdiction and is better handled by the Federal Trade Commission. The FTC is undertaking a probe.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt, however, wants his agency's four members to vote next week on whether to conduct a probe.
But Chong asked that the item be stricken from the agenda for the FCC's June 19 public meeting. A commissioner has the power to remove the item through such a request.

"The issue of advertising practices by the hard liquor industry would be best left in the hands of our sister agency, the FTC, to address these issues in its ongoing proceedings," Chong said in a statement.
"If further action is warranted, Congress is in the best position to decide what government action may be appropriate."
Quello echoed that sentiment in a separate statement.
The liquor industry last year abandoned a decades-old voluntary ban on marketing over the airwaves. President Clinton has called on distillers to discontinue the practice.
